sources.entry: Ollama - Get up and running with Llama 3.3, DeepSeek-R1, Phi-4, Gemma 3, and other large language models. (Source Code) MIT Docker/Python
Ollama | Run Llama, Qwen, Gemma, DeepSeek and other open models locally with a simple API

summary.one_liner: Ollama is a tool for downloading, running, and serving open large language models locally (and optionally in the cloud), with a CLI, a REST API, and Python and JavaScript libraries.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes installing Ollama on macOS, Windows, and Linux via install scripts or manual download, and provides an official Docker image (ollama/ollama on Docker Hub). Running "ollama" in a terminal prompts the user to run a model or connect Ollama to existing agents and apps. The CLI can run models such as Gemma 4 with "ollama run gemma4". A REST API handles running and managing models, and official Python (ollama-python) and JavaScript (ollama-js) libraries wrap it. The "ollama launch" command starts integrations such as Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI, DeepSeek Harness, Droid, OpenCode, and OpenClaw. The README also lists a large community section of chat UIs, editor plugins, SDKs, agent frameworks, RAG tools, and deployment packages that integrate with Ollama.
use_cases: run open-weight LLMs locally on your own machine
serve a local model API for apps and scripts
chat with a local model from the terminal
power a self-hosted ChatGPT-style web interface
use a local model as a coding assistant in editors
build retrieval-augmented generation over your own documents
how_to_run: curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh (macOS/Linux; the README shows this command without the URL, so confirm on the project site)
irm https://ollama.com/install.ps1 | iex (Windows; URL not shown in README)
notable: Single tool covers CLI, REST API, and official Python and JavaScript libraries
Official Docker image on Docker Hub
Launches integrations with coding agents and assistants via 'ollama launch'
Large community ecosystem of chat UIs, editor plugins, SDKs, and deployment packages listed in the README
Runs models built on the llama.cpp project
caveats: README does not state hardware requirements; model size and speed depend on the local machine
The README says models are available 'locally or in the cloud', so some features may need an Ollama account or cloud access (not detailed in README)
Install commands in the README are shown without full URLs in some places, so verify download sources before running
keywords: run ai on my own computer
